verdict.rationale: Missive documents its own natural-language surfaces. An in-app AI assistant composes, replies, and translates, answers how-to questions from the docs, and runs sessions that can create drafts. An official MCP server also lets Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor act on conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts through chat, for example by summarizing the inbox and drafting replies. However, the evidence does not establish that natural-language commands can drive the product broadly (assigning, labeling, archiving, rules, settings), and every source is vendor changelog or marketing copy. missing for 10: documented breadth of in-app assistant actions beyond drafting, composing and doc Q&A; natural-language control of core inbox operations; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: External AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now connect to Missive through the Model Context Protocol and act on your conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts, with the permissions you choose.
Ask Claude to summarize your inbox and draft replies without leaving the chat
Quickly compose, reply, and translate messages with AI directly in Missive.
Ask how a feature works, how to set up a rule, or where a setting lives. The answer comes straight from the Missive documentation instead of a guess.
Drafts created outside the composer, by the assistant, by a rule, or through the API and MCP server, now resolve {{ user.name }} and {{ user.email }} from your organization profile
